title: auditor-question-bank-and-gap-briefing-rbacv2-siem-pipeline
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working brief is intended for the upcoming external SOC 2 / ISO 27001 auditor engagements. Focus: RBAC v2 enforcement model, audit-log schema and retention, SIEM export pipeline (evidence automation), and a compact bank of anticipated auditor questions with concise evidence pointers and gaps.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- RBAC v2 has been rolled out to all production control planes; enforcement gaps remain in legacy migration paths and a small set of internal admin scripts.
- Audit log schema is standardized; primary gap is bounded sampling policy for high-volume endpoints and a missing immutable WORM export for long-term retention beyond 1 year.
- SIEM export (Splunk/Elastic) pipeline exists with daily export artifacts; automation coverage for evidence packaging is ~85%.
- Immediate action items for auditor readiness: complete the RBAC migration for two internal tools (sec-owned), finalize WORM export design, and add two acceptance tests in the evidence pipeline.

Control mapping overview (short):
- SOC 2 CC6/ISO A.9 (access control): RBAC v2 roles -> control families mapped; we maintain role definition docs, role assignment workflows, and periodic access review artifacts. Evidence: role-definition YAMLs, access review spreadsheets, IAM change tickets.
- SOC 2 CC7/ISO A.12 (logging & monitoring): System audit logs, retention policy, SIEM ingestion proofs. Evidence: SIEM ingest dashboards, stored export bundles, log schema spec.
- SOC 2 CC5/ISO A.16 (incident response): Alerting and playbooks integrated into SIEM with runbooks. Evidence: incident runbooks, postmortems, alert-to-ticket correlation samples.

Audit log schema (canonical fields) — include in evidence bundle:
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- service (e.g., api-gateway, auth-service, runtime)
- event_type (access_grant, token_issue, token_revoke, model_infer, config_change)
- actor_id (RBAC principal id)
- actor_role (computed at event time)
- resource_type (route, model, deployment, secret)
- resource_id
- action (read, write, impersonate, escalate, auth)
- outcome (success, denied, error)
- request_id (traceable to trace/span)
- kv_diff (optional, redacted)
- ip_address (redacted per PII policy)
- raw_message_hash (sha256)
Example line: 2024-07-14T21:12:03Z | auth-service | access_grant | u-1245 | org-admin | deployment | dep-03 | read | success | r-8f3a | - | 1.2.3.4 | 9a1b...

Evidence automation / SIEM export pipeline (current flow):
1) App services produce structured JSON audit events to Kafka topic audits-prod (schema validated by schema-registry).
2) Consumers enrich events with actor_role (from RBAC cache) and attach raw_message_hash.
3) A daily ETL job writes partitioned exports to object storage (s3://redwood-evidence/siem_exports/YYYY-MM-DD/).
4) SIEM forwarder ingests from the ETL landing zone into Splunk index:redwood-audit.
5) Evidence packager (python lambda) pulls index query results, applies redaction rules, creates manifest.json, signs bundle with KMS, and uploads to evidence-store for auditor retrieval.

Known pipeline gaps (impact + remediation):
- Gap: high-volume endpoints (model infer logs) are sampled at 1% by default; auditors may question sufficiency for traceability.
  - Impact: inability to provide exhaustive model-infer traces for large date ranges.
  - Mitigation: provide targeted unsampled capture for specific rolling windows (ad-hoc capture) and augment with model request id correlation to billing records. Planned: increase sampling to 5% for next quarter and add evidence-level sampling justification doc. Owner: Rajat Singh.
- Gap: no immutable (WORM) export for >1 year retention required by some ISO interpretations.
  - Impact: long-term archival evidence may be challenged.
  - Mitigation: design WORM export to customer vaults or cold storage; short-term workaround is weekly signed bundles. Owner: Lena Ortiz.
- Gap: internal admin CLI scripts bypass RBAC enforcement in legacy path /ops/admin-sync.
  - Impact: control exception.
  - Mitigation: quarantine scripts, require token exchange flow, and add unit tests. Owner: Owen Park.

Auditor Q&A bank (likely questions and prepared artifacts):
Q: How do you ensure the actor_role in the logs represents the actual permission set at time-of-event?
A: We enrich events with a snapshot role computed from RBAC cache during processing; evidence: RBAC cache flush logs, enrichment consumer code link, sample enriched event lines (examples included in bundle). Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbacv2-config/pull/212

Q: Can you show proof of tamper-proofing for audit bundles?
A: Bundles are signed with KMS keys (asymmetric keypair), raw_message_hash stored in manifest, and signatures attached. Evidence: manifest.json example, KMS key rotation policy, sample signature verification transcript.

Q: What is your log retention policy and how do you handle deletion requests?
A: Retention is 1 year in hot index, 3 years in cold object-store (signed bundles weekly); deletion requests follow legal/data-privacy workflow — we redact PII in logs on ingest using a deterministic hash. Evidence: retention-policy.md, S3 lifecycle policy, redact-job run logs.

Q: How do you reconcile RBAC changes to historical logs for audit?
A: We store actor_role (snapshot) at event time; changes to role definitions are recorded as config_change events with before/after diffs. Evidence: config-change event samples, role-change Jira tickets and timestamps.

Q: Provide sampling justification for model-infer events?
A: Sampling policy is risk-based: high-volume, low-risk events are sampled; critical actions (auth, config_change, access_grant) are fully recorded. We provide sampling math and a mapping of when unsampled capture is triggered. Evidence: sampling-policy.md and recent unsampled-capture run.

Acceptance criteria for evidence bundles (auditor-facing):
- Bundle manifest includes date range, query used, sample rates applied, signer id, and bundle signature.
- Every event has traceable request_id and raw_message_hash.
- Redaction rules applied with audit log of redactions (what removed and why).
- Linked config and timeline for RBAC role definitions in effect for the date range.

Playbook for live auditor session (30–45 min):
- Intro (5 min): scope & artifacts we will show.
- RBAC walkthrough (10 min): role definition doc, role assignment workflow demo (screenshot), and one role-change PR timeline.
- Logs & SIEM (15 min): run a sample Splunk query to show enrichment and manifest creation; demonstrate bundle signature verification locally.
- Q&A and evidence hand-off (10 min).
Prep checklist (owners):
- Freeze RBAC role docs for the demo window (Owner: Maya Chen).
- Run an unsampled capture for a 2-hour window and stash the bundle (Owner: Rajat Singh).
- Generate signed weekly export for the last 90 days and validate signatures (Owner: Lena Ortiz).
- Produce a redaction audit sample for PII removal (Owner: Owen Park).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Confirm retention policy alignment with ISO auditor expectation for our region (EMEA may ask for 3-year immutable retention). Owner: Legal + Lena.
- Final decision on whether to adopt block-level WORM or signed weekly bundles as long-term approach (deadline: 2024-12-01).

Notes to self / informal bits (working doc style):
- Include a short script to pull request all artifacts into a temp S3 path and email auditors a signed download token.
- Keep a zip with minimal PII redaction examples — auditors like seeing both raw and redacted paired.
- Record a 3-minute screencast of signature verification steps and attach to evidence bundle.

Recent related artifacts (quick refs):
- PR: rbacv2-config/pull/212 (enrichment consumer changes)
- JIRA: SEC-487 (WORM export epic)
- Confluence: Audit Evidence Index (link above)

Action items (single-line):
- Rajat: increase sampling for next quarter + run unsampled capture (due 2024-11-12).
- Lena: finalize WORM design doc and cost estimate (due 2024-11-20).
- Owen: lock down admin scripts and add enforcement tests (due 2024-11-07).
- Maya: schedule dry-run with internal auditors (due 2024-11-10).

End of doc.
